desc: Parse input efficiently using sys.stdin for speed given large constraints.
Extract positions of 1s in A (sources) and positions of 1s in B (targets) for each test case.
Finalize theory: reachable iff counts OK, monotone surjective assignment with nonincreasing gaps; answer = min over assignments of max displacement; reachability in k = max disp ops holds.
Replace ok(k) with the provably correct feasibility check (forward-minimal r, backward-maximal s, coverage greedy) and integrate into solve().
Stress-test against brute force (BFS over configurations) for small N: confirmed reduction theory is correct; found current ok(k) greedy is broken (forward/backward interval coverage argument fails).
Implement the cut-based `ok(k)`: precompute L_j, R_j (target-index window within distance k of p_j) via bisect; greedy left-to-right grouping with cut-gap constraints; prove via exchange argument.
Re-run the BFS stress test over all N ≤ 7 (and random N ≤ 10 with many trials) until zero mismatches, including edge cases: m = n, m = N, single piece, targets at extremes, k = 0.
Verify the three sample answers (3, −1, 5) through the fixed checker.
Confirm complexity (O(N log^2 N) total) and final stdin/stdout wiring.
